## TL;DR

I exercised the Release chooser and hand-run restart notice against the app from this task worktree, using Playwright route stubs for mutation endpoints. The chooser copy names the exact tag and clearly distinguishes automatic publish from Notify me; Notify says the operator reviews and presses Publish. A pending publish survived a browser reload after reopening the cut panel, and its Cancel action reached the cancel endpoint. The tests also cover Notify-only behavior and failed-draft fail-closed behavior. I found no product defect to fix or larger defect to file.

The update/restart notice rendered for hand-run, launchd, and systemd fixtures at 1440 and 390 pixels in light and dark themes. I inspected all captures. Hand-run shows “Restart now” and explains the recorded serve flags and port; launchd and systemd show the restart actions without printing a service command.

## Work and rationale

This is a verification task, so I kept the branch source unchanged. I ran `just serve-noauth 7371` from the assigned task worktree. The recipe confirmed it was serving the preview build at localhost port 7371. I did not use the main checkout. The Releases page was available and exposed the cut panel; its actual release endpoints were stubbed in Playwright for the interactive publish path. The stubs returned a running AI draft and a waiting publish record; release mutation calls were blocked or counted instead of reaching real release code. No release was cut, published, pushed, or tagged, and I did not click any restart action.

In the cut panel I opened “Generate with AI” and read the chooser at both choices. The Notify wording says the draft will be filled in for review and that the user presses Publish; it does not claim RepoOS will publish. The Publish choice says it will publish the exact suggested tag and explains the guard conditions that prevent publishing if drafting or checks fail. I selected Publish in the browser, observed the pending state for v0.5.90, reloaded, reopened the cut panel, and confirmed that the waiting state remained. I clicked the Cancel button inside the pending promise card and confirmed the DELETE cancellation request was recorded. The stub recorded one notes request and zero release mutation requests.

To cover the Notify selection and failed-draft boundary, I also ran the repository’s existing test seams. The focused UI tests assert that selecting Notify sends `whenReady: "notify"`, fills the notes, and does not create a pending automatic publish. The server tests assert that Notify never starts a release and that a failed draft publishes nothing while recording the reason. The tests include cancellation and the guard-failure cases as well.

For the restart notice I served fake update-status and release-available payloads. Hand-run, launchd, and systemd were each captured at 1440×900 and 390×900, in both themes. I inspected each PNG individually. The copy and controls fit at mobile width. The hand-run notice exposes the active “Restart now” action and recorded-port explanation; supervised states present one restart pair and avoid misleading shell commands. I left the action untouched.

Screenshots and the Playwright harness are in the ignored evidence directory `.repoos/qa-pass-1168/`; the restart captures are named by supervisor, theme, and viewport. The chooser and pending-state captures are there too. They document the QA states without adding generated images or harness code to the branch.

## Approaches tried

The first direct Vitest invocation used `bunx vitest` and failed during Vite import analysis because it bypassed the repository’s Vue test configuration. I reran through `bun run test`, which invokes the project wrapper and loaded the Vue plugin correctly. The focused suites passed: release-when-ready and release UI tests (49 tests), followed by automatic-publish tests (18 tests).

The first Playwright pass used a generic Cancel locator and hit the panel’s close action rather than the promise’s Cancel. I corrected it to scope the click to `[data-test-id="release-panel-auto-publish"]`; the subsequent pass recorded one cancellation request. This was a test-script targeting issue, not an application defect.

## Challenges and blockers

The task worktree’s current branch is behind the configured main release line, so the live server disables the actual release button. That is useful protection for this pass. Playwright provided a ready status for the UI flow while intercepting all release API writes, so no real tag or publish path was invoked. I did not attempt a real server restart.

The browser host tool was unavailable, so I used Playwright, which the task explicitly permits. I did not make or attach a defect screenshot because I found no defect.

## Key learnings

The new release chooser’s safety wording is clear in the UI, and the pending automatic-publish record is server-owned across reloads. The cancellation control needs to be targeted within its card when other Cancel buttons are present in the drawer. The update notice differentiates hand-run from supervised servers in its action content without exposing platform-specific service commands.

No code change was warranted.
